neutral_facts.value: The prosecution case was that a dead body was found in a house in Delhi. The dead body was identified as the husband of PW-23. The wife of the deceased stated that her husband had in possession a licensed revolver, a mobile phone SIM (9871879824), and a sum of Rs.3 lakhs when he left Chandigarh for Delhi to negotiate a settlement. During the investigation, it was found that the mobile phone (9871879824) was used on a mobile handset bearing IMEI no.35136304044030. Further investigation revealed that the said IMEI was used for the mobile phone SIM 9818480558 belonging to the accused-appellant immediately after the murder of the victim-deceased. This helped the police in apprehending the appellant and in recovery of three mobile handsets, one of which bore the IMEI no.35136304044030. The police also recovered from the appellant, the licensed revolver of the deceased. The amount of Rs.3 lakhs was not found, however, there was a deposit entry in the account of the appellant of Rs.9000 two days after the murder. Based on circumstantial evidence, the trial court convicted the appellant under Sections 302 and 404 IPC and sentenced him to undergo rigorous imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Rs.50000 for the offence punishable under Section 302, IPC. The appellant was also sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for three years and to pay Rs5000 for offence punishable under Section 404, IPC. He was, however, acquitted of the charges framed against him under Sections 380 and 452, IPC. The High Court dismissed the appeal against conviction, however, modified the sentence inasmuch as in the event of non-payment of fine imposed on the appellant for the offence punishable under Section 302, IPC, the High Court reduced the period of imprisonment in lieu thereof from three years to six months.

key_evidence_accepted.value: The evidence produced by the prosecution was based on the irrefutable fact that every mobile handset has an exclusive IMEI number. The use of mobile handset of the victim on which the accused made calls from his own registered mobile phone (SIM) immediately after the occurrence of the murder was a legitimate basis for the identification of the accused. The revolver of the victim was also recovered from the accused.

quotes.text: The evidence produced by the prosecution was based on the irrefutable fact that every mobile handset has an exclusive IMEI number. Every time a mobile handset is used for making a call, besides recording the number of the call as well as the person called, the IMEI numbers of the handsets used are also recorded by the service provider.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused-appellant was implicated based on the use of a mobile handset bearing IMEI No.35136304044030, which was traced through call records and the recovery of the revolver of the deceased from the accused. The evidence included the deceased's mobile phone SIM number becoming dead on the date of murder, the use of the IMEI number to trace the accused, and the recovery of the revolver and mobile handset from the accused.

quotes.text: The prosecution case was that a dead body was found in a house in Delhi. On enquiry, it was found that dead body was of husband of PW-23.

The police also recovered from the appellant, the licensed revolver of the deceased. The amount of Rs.3 lakhs was not found, however, there was a deposit entry in the account of the appellant of Rs.9000 two days after the murder.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the prosecution fabricated a false story to implicate the accused, pointing out discrepancies in the evidence of PW23, such as the call records indicating incoming calls instead of outgoing calls from the deceased's SIM number. They also suggested that the revolver and mobile handset were planted on the accused to implicate him.

quotes.text: It was contended for the appellant, that the factum of tracing the appellant from the mobile phone (SIM) of the deceased was a complete concoction at the hands of the investigating agency.
It was also sought to be suggested, that if the investigating agency's theory of reaching the appellant was based on the call details of mobile phone (SIM) no.9871879824, the same was unacceptable.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that every mobile handset has an exclusive IMEI number, and that the use of such numbers in call records can be scientific evidence to establish the accused's connection to the crime.

quotes.text: Every mobile handset has an exclusive IMEI number. No two mobile handsets have the same IMEI number.

Every time a mobile handset is used for making a call, besides recording the number of the caller as well as the person called, the IMEI numbers of the handsets used are also recorded by the service provider.

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed based on the overwhelming evidence produced by the prosecution, including the recovery of the revolver and mobile handset from the accused, and the use of the IMEI number to trace the accused, which established the accused's nexus with the crime.

quotes.text: The prosecution has brought home the charges as have been found to be established against the accused-appellant, by the trial court as also by the High Court.
The accused-appellant was arrested on 6.8.2005. The nexus of the accused-appellant with the deceased at the time of occurrence stood fully substantiated from the said SIM/IMEI details.
